subject: environmental-science
title: Effective Population Size
welcome_lead: Genes you cannot see decide whether species survive — meet Ne.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on effective population size and genetic drift.
final_note: Effective Ne is usually a fraction of the census count — and it controls drift.

concepts.def: Number of breeders contributing equally to next generation.
Total count of individuals; usually >> Ne.
Random change in allele frequencies, stronger in small populations.
Reduced fitness due to homozygosity of deleterious recessives.
Proportion of heterozygous loci; measure of genetic diversity.
Minimum Ne 50 to avoid inbreeding short-term, 500 long-term (Franklin/Soulé).

walkthroughs.body_html: Drift loss of heterozygosity per generation is 1/(2Ne). Small Ne means fast drift and high inbreeding.
Ne = (4·Nm·Nf)/(Nm+Nf) for skewed sex ratios. Variance in reproductive success further reduces Ne.
Conservation aims for Ne ≥ 50 to avoid immediate inbreeding and Ne ≥ 500 to maintain long-term adaptive potential.

options: Minimum Ne for short- and long-term viability
